items.text: Round 2 decisions D7=A (two-table schema), D8=B (requireAdminOrService with LPBS_SERVICE_SECRET), D9=B (defer promote API/CLI/UI; orchestrator + schema accept arbitrary channels), and D10=B (Postgres advisory lock per profile) were incorporated into the plan. Section 8 now lists D7-D10 under 'Settled in round 2 workshop' and removes the 'To be settled' subsection.

Phase 2 in section 7 was tightened to spell out the D8 auth wiring: DM holds LPBS_SERVICE_SECRET as an env var (same pattern S2D already uses for presign/commit/apply) and sends it as the service header that LPBS's requireAdminOrService middleware expects. A startup warning when the secret is unset is called out in the auth-mismatch risk row.

Phase 2 advisory-lock detail (D10=B) made concrete: pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('release:' || profile_id)) is acquired before release-record allocation, held for the orchestration transaction, and on contention returns HTTP 409 with a {error:'release_in_flight', profile_id:...} payload. A new unit test in section 9 covers parallel-start serialization and lock release on transaction end.

Phase 5 was tightened per round 2 i1: S2D already carries Config.Version → ReleaseVersion and Provenance.GitCommitHash end-to-end, so the S2D-side change is just two new fields (ReleaseID, Channel) threaded through PublishPipelineRequest → DeployConfig → existing lpbs_client.go plumbing. AppKey/RemoteProfile/UpdateURL already exist on PublishDeployConfig; DM populates them in Phase 2 and they pass through unchanged. This keeps Phase 5 under a day of work.

D9=B is reflected by making the channel column free-text TEXT with DEFAULT 'stable' (no CHECK constraint), and by having the orchestrator and CLI accept --channel <name> for any value today. The promoted_from_release_id column is reserved on the releases table so the future promote handler/CLI/UI lands without a migration. A new section-9 test asserts arbitrary-channel acceptance end-to-end. The promote flow itself remains explicitly out of scope (sections 4 and 12).

Section 12 grew two new prohibitions that bind the round-2 decisions: do NOT use per-app X-Update-Key or admin-only auth on /deploy-readiness (D8=B pins it to requireAdminOrService); do NOT use an in-memory mutex for release concurrency (D10=B pins it to a Postgres advisory lock so the guard survives multi-node deploys). Section 13 acceptance criterion 8 was updated to state all ten decisions D1-D10 must be resolved with no TBDs remaining.

All five readiness dimensions remain at 3/3/3/3/3. The plan's TBD set is empty, the scope is bounded across four scenarios, every decision has a settled answer threaded into the relevant plan section, and every gap (concurrency, dry-run exclusion, hard-fail verify, auth, arbitrary channels) has at least one corresponding test in section 9. No outstanding workshop decisions remain — the item is ready to be moved to status 'ready' for queueing.

plan_updates: Section 6 #2 added the explicit auth model 'requireAdminOrService using LPBS_SERVICE_SECRET; per D2=A and D8=B' to the LPBS upload-readiness step and 'profile-scoped advisory lock per D10=B' to the release-allocation step. Section 6 #3 added 'adopted verbatim per D7=A' to the release-record schema sub-bullet and a new sub-bullet noting the orchestrator accepts arbitrary channel values per D9=B. Section 5 added a new row to the LPBS table calling out api/server.go requireAdminOrService as the auth pattern the new endpoint adopts, and a note under the S2D table reflecting round 2 i1's two-field reduction. Section 7 Phase 1 added the D9-driven note that channel is free-text TEXT with no CHECK constraint. Phase 2 spelled out the D8 secret wiring (env var, peer-service pattern) and the D10 advisory-lock semantics (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock, 409 payload, auto-release on transaction end). Phase 3 noted releases.start defaults channel to default_channel and accepts --channel <name>. Phase 5 was rewritten to reflect the two-fields-only S2D change. Section 8 moved D7-D10 from 'To be settled in round 2' to 'Settled in round 2 workshop' with a one-line rationale each, and removed the 'To be settled' subsection entirely. Section 9 added unit tests for advisory-lock concurrency (D10), arbitrary-channel acceptance (D9), and a new integration test asserting DM sends the LPBS_SERVICE_SECRET header on /deploy-readiness (D8). Section 10 grew validation checklist items for the new tests. Section 11 risk rows for concurrency, orphans, auth, and promote-forward-compat were rewritten to reference the specific D-decisions. Section 12 added two new prohibitions (no per-app key / admin-only on /deploy-readiness, no in-memory mutex). Section 13 acceptance criterion 8 was tightened to require all ten decisions D1-D10 resolved.
